title: Review liquor licence limits so they target harm, not competitors
action: Review restrictions on who may sell alcohol and how many licences are issued, so that they target alcohol-related harm (for example through conditions on high-risk outlets) rather than protecting existing licensees from new competitors.
why: Licence freezes and limits on which retailers may sell packaged alcohol keep new and smaller competitors out and entrench the largest chains.

evidence.source: NSW Productivity Commission White Paper 2021: Rebooting the economy
evidence.quote: Review the restrictions on supermarkets and other retailers selling packaged alcohol for off-premises consumption

evidence.source: NSW Productivity Commission White Paper 2021: Rebooting the economy
evidence.quote: Such a review would ensure liquor licensing restrictions are not 'more about competitors than public safety'

tradeoffs: Restrictions such as the Northern Territory's takeaway moratorium were adopted to reduce alcohol harm in communities with high rates of it; a review must weigh those health benefits, which this framework does not measure.
